lead: Bakersfield plumbing deals with hard water, intense heat and slab homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Bakersfield.
risk: hard water scale, slab leaks and water heater wear
risk_short: hard water, slab leaks and water heaters
why: Older areas such as Westchester and Oleander-Sunset have homes from the 1930s to the 1950s with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron or clay drains. Seven Oaks and Rosedale were built mostly after 1990.
Most homes sit on slabs, so supply leaks under the floor are common. Summer heat and hard water wear out water heaters.
utility: California Water Service and City of Bakersfield Water Resources
water: Bakersfield is served by several water providers, mainly California Water Service and the city's Water Resources Department. Supply is mostly groundwater plus Kern River water. It is hard.
tips: Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown, Westchester, Oleander-Sunset, Seven Oaks, Rosedale, Haggin Oaks, East Bakersfield and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Bakersfield Building Division, and plumbing contractors need a CSLB license with a C-36 classification.

faq.a: Bakersfield has more than one water provider. California Water Service and the city's Water Resources Department serve most homes. Your water bill shows which one you have.
